situation:
You are to assume the role of general manager of OLIVE & EMBER, a quick-serve Mediterranean restaurant in the entertainment district of a mid-sized city. The regional vice president (judge), who took over the brand a year ago, has asked you to recommend what the store should do about its weekend hours.

Olive & Ember lost money for two years before new leadership arrived, and the turnaround now rests on two commitments the store has already made. The first is its lease with the district landlord, which requires the dining room to stay open until two in the morning on Friday and Saturday, a clause the landlord wrote to keep the block busy after the theaters let out.

The second is a catering contract with the hotel across the street, which books the store's kitchen and crew for a plated event every Friday evening and has become the steadiest and most profitable work the store does. The same crew and the same ovens cannot cover both. A crew that plates the hotel event cannot then run the dining room until two, and after midnight the store serves fewer than a dozen guests an hour.

The regional vice president (judge) wants a recommendation. Staying open until two as the lease requires means giving up the hotel's Friday events and the steady revenue the turnaround was built on. Closing at eleven to keep the hotel contract puts the store in breach of the lease clause and gives the landlord grounds to raise the rent at renewal.

You will present your recommendation to the regional vice president (judge) in the regional vice president's (judge) office. The regional vice president (judge) will begin by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the regional vice president's (judge) questions, the regional vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of regional vice president of OLIVE & EMBER, having taken over the brand a year ago. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the general manager (participant) to recommend what the store should do about its weekend hours, given that the lease with the district landlord and the catering contract with the hotel across the street cannot both be kept. You want to hear which commitment the store should honor, what the store gains and gives up either way, and how the choice fits what the brand is trying to be.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who does this decision land hardest on?
How would you explain it to them?
